newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor is contemplating his future after Australia's 29 run loss to Pakistan in Hobart yesterday. Australia is now at the bottom of the Carlton and United series, having lost 10 of 12 one day matches and five international games in a row. However, it still leads the Test series 2-1. Page 18.

Members of the Victorian Jockeys Association and officials from the Victoria Racing Club will meet today to discuss further developments in the nationwide pay dispute. Both sides are hopeful the pay claims will be settled soon following the intervention of Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett. The dispute has caused fines to be levelled at jockeys Australia-wide and the cancellation of the World Jockeys Championship. Page 18.

Top West Indies cricket batsmen have been performing below their potential, despite the team's success in its Australian tour. Robert Samuels, Adrian Griffith and Roland Holder all had low scores in the West Indies win over the Australian CountryX1 at Toowoomba's heritage oval yesterday. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Top seed and world number three women's tennis player Arantxa Sanchez Vicario blamed herself for her surprise loss to American Amy Frazier 6-3, 6-3 in the first round of the Sydney International yesterday. Other upsets included Jennifer Capriati's defeat over Chanda Rubin 6-3, 4-6, 6-3. Page 50

Adrienne Cahalan, the skipper of the all-women crew of Elle Racing, Australia's first entry in the Whitbread around-the-world race, has resigned, as has fellow sailor Vanessa Dudley. Cahalan cited a lack of funding as the reason for her resignation. She will be replaced by American Joan Touchette. Page 49.

At the Australian skydiving championships above the New South Wales border town of Corowa this week, Michael Kelaher, Jonathan King and Mick Forrest won the sitflying division. This is the first time sitflying has been included in the championships - a combination of freestyle elements and new techniques that lock team members together. Page 48.
THE AGE

Winner of the 1991 British Open, Australian golfer Ian Baker-Finch, began an attempted comeback with a tournament practice round, his first since the British Open last July. Baker-Finch has suffered bad form in the last two years leading him to try a career as a TV commentator. He believes however that he can again be top-ranked, despite notifying the US golf authorities that he would resign his 1997 membership for the season. Page 6.

Carl Lewis, the 20th century's greatest track and field athlete, is expected to participate in the 1997 Athletics Australia Grand Prix series. In an announcement to be made today, Lewis who has won nine Olympic gold medals, is expected to compete in the sprints competition only. Also competing will be Ireland's Sonia O'Sullivan, the 1995 female athletics athlete of the year. Page 6.

Monica Seles has decided not to play in the Ford Australian Open because of to a finger injury. Seles who won the title last year, suffered the injury at an exhibition match last November. Organisers, while disappointed said the women's field would stil be a strong one with Steffi Graf, Martina Hingis, Mary Pierce and Jennifer Capriati all competing. Page 6.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Rules coaches have supported a proposal from national umpires coach Bill Deller to reduce the time-wasting tactic of "stacks on the mill". The proposal, yet to be discussed by the AFL Commission, would allow for time-on at a field bounce from the moment the umpire blows his whistle until the ball is back in play, stopping tactics such as players diving on to the ball. Page 78.

Australian tennis player Patrick Rafter will apologise to fellow Australian Richard Fromberg after Rafter asked Fromberg to replay a point in their match at the Sydney International tennis tournament yesterday. Rafter, who won the match, questioned a shot from Fromberg in the second set, thinking Fromberg had hit a ball through the net. Fromberg eventually won the point. Page 77.

Pakistan cricket captain Wasim Akram took a gamble on his team's late replacement Mujahad Jamshed and Ijaz Ahmed Sr, who between them took two of Australia's vital wickets in the match at Hobart. While Pakistan appeared to do everything wrong in the game they defeated Australia by playing a more mature game. Page 74.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The North Sydney Bears rugby league club refuses to make public any disciplinary action it will take against its players who were guilty of misbehaving at the one day cricket international at the Sydney Cricket Ground on New Year's Day. However, ARL chief Ken Arthurson says Norths should release details of the investigation into the incident so the public knows justice has been done. Page 102.

Australian tennis player Rachel McQuillan yesterday unexpectedly defeated Dutch player and seventh seed Brenda Schultz-McCarthy in the first round of the Sydney International tennis tournament. McQuillan, who entered the event on a wildcard, was able to handle Schultz-McCarthy's serve after a strong training regime which included playing against Newcastle's strongest young male players. Page 98.

Halfway through the Ericsson Cup soccer championship, it looks like the Brisbane Strikers and Perth Glory could meet in the grand final, despite early failures for debutantes Perth. Perth Glory's entry into the national competition came a year early, but with average home crowds of 9799, their entry is paying dividends. Page 93.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
